title: Help Scout alternatives for B2B teams outgrowing email | Pylon
summary: When email support can't keep up with growing teams, it's time to explore Help Scout alternatives built for cross-channel, cross-team B2B support.
body_markdown:
Help Scout can help launch a startup’s support team, but many companies outgrow its email-first approach. For B2B support teams, company growth comes with high volumes of customer conversations across multiple channels, like Slack and Microsoft Teams.


When those messages come from accounts with multiple points of contact who expect you to remember their context and take multiple actions that each have their own workflows to resolve their query, B2B support at scale can get stressful without the right tools.


In this article, we’ll look at five Help Scout alternatives for B2B teams looking for an omnichannel, cross-team support platform upgrade. We’ll explore the strengths of each option and the best criteria to use to evaluate them.


## Why B2B teams look for Help Scout alternatives


Issue view in Pylon


Here are common signs that it might be time to move on from Help Scout:


- **Rising case complexity.** Help Scout’s shared inbox is great for resolving a few simple queries at a time. It’s less useful when you work with multiple teams per account, which all come with different needs. When you’re also taking on new cases that require escalations to the dev team, approval layers with internal leads and customer stakeholders, and enterprise customer relationships that need proactive monitoring and a human touch, you may find you need an AI-powered system that can keep up with changes as they happen.
- **Fragmented customer context.** As of[November 2025](https://docs.helpscout.com/article/1740-whats-new-with-company-management) , Plus and Pro plan Help Scout users can see all points of contact at a company and your recent conversations. As your organization scales, finding information like how your dev team resolved a bug or what your support lead told the customer the last time they spoke means tracking down and reading all those messages to get context. That can lead to slower response times and longer[time to resolution](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/time-to-resolution) .
- **Stacked AI costs.** Advanced features are only available on Help Scout’s higher-tier paid plans, and it charges a separate fee for every issue its AI agent resolves. That per-resolution fee for AI Answers makes it hard for teams to predict their costs and can quickly exceed your budget as volumes and complexity increase.
- **Thin native reporting.** Help Scout doesn’t offer many reporting tools, and the dashboard is quite basic. You can generate seven reports (grouped by communication channel, company, customer happiness, and docs, or knowledge base questions). You would have to export data and build custom dashboards to get detailed analysis of account health metrics, SLA breaches, and resolution times, for instance.


## Top Help Scout alternatives compared


Here’s a comparison of the best Help Scout alternatives for growing B2B teams. We’ll look at when each one would be the best fit for a team migrating from Help Scout, and any major limitations they have.


### Pylon


**Best for:** B2B teams with complex support needs.


[Pylon](https://www.usepylon.com/) is an agentic support platform built specifically for complex B2B customer support. It pulls together omnichannel communication on every platform your customers use with automations and collaboration between team members and AI agents.


It comes with six kinds of[AI Agents](https://www.usepylon.com/b2b-support) to help your support team resolve issues across every channel:


- **Assist Agent.** Safely pulls information from any internal note, document, or conversation to guide your team’s decisions.
- **Background Agents.** Outsources menial tasks, like running skills and updating systems, to free up your team’s time for complex tickets.
- **Support Agent.** Handles customer conversations using public information, and shares context when it’s time to escalate to a team member.
- **Slack Agent.** Gives team members full access to Pylon directly in Slack with just a tag.
- **Skills.** Runs pre-set workflows (including from integrations and custom tools) using one command, not a dozen.
- **Connectors.** Links Pylon to your other software via MCP or custom API for a more robust response network when the context is necessary.


Together, all six create a strong agentic workflow that doesn’t require you to give up the control you need to care for enterprise relationships.


Pylon is a great solution for teams managing complex cross-team support issues and accounts with multiple stakeholders, and it has dedicated guidance on[migrating from Help Scout](https://support.usepylon.com/articles/4400330627-migrating-from-help-scout) . If your team mostly works through email and doesn’t need account context, agentic workflows, or omnichannel visibility, Help Scout’s simpler features may be a better fit.


### Zendesk


**Best for:** Enterprise-forward teams that want to integrate multiple programs.


[Zendesk](https://www.zendesk.com/) is made for large companies looking for a flexible support platform that’s ready to scale with your team. It’s an established platform that also offers a marketplace with over 1,000 integrations and AI agents and copilots to speed up issue resolution (compared to Help Scout’s approximately 100 options and limited native automation).


However, Zendesk lacks native Slack support, so it’s not a great fit for B2B companies that need to combine insights from every channel. Zendesk also charges extra per-resolution and per-agent add-on fees for AI agents, so costs can climb quickly. That makes it less than ideal for B2B teams that center task automation in their scaling strategy.


### Front


**Best for:** Smaller teams with longstanding customer relationships.


[Front](https://front.com/) can be a good fit for teams that like the email-first, conversation-based approach of Help Scout but are ready to take the next step toward automation. With internal notes, assignments, and shared customer context visibility, Front's AI can handle simple queries, and escalate to your team when it can’t pull from public knowledge.


Note, however, that important features like Front’s AI Copilot are limited to higher tiers of paid plans. It also charges separate fees every time its AI agent routes, hands off, or resolves a customer inquiry, which can make it expensive for B2B support that regularly collaborate and escalate across teams. If you’re just getting started with automating your support team, look into Front, but it isn’t a great fit for B2B teams with established AI workflows looking to scale.


### Freshdesk


**Best for:** Companies that work in B2B and B2C contexts.


If you want a like-for-like alternative to Help Scout, look into[Freshdesk](https://www.freshworks.com/freshdesk/) , Freshworks’ AI-powered customer support tool. It adds an AI agent to email inboxes to answer simple queries while consolidating the responses into one dashboard, an AI Copilot to run workflows, and AI Insights into key operational metrics.


Freshdesk’s pricing is more predictable than Help Scout’s. All its paid plans come with 500 free AI sessions, and additional sessions are bundled instead of charged per resolution. However, heavier AI users will still face higher costs if they need multiple bundles per month. It also doesn’t fit the needs of a complex B2B system because its AI Insights are relatively limited, and account context is sparse at lower paid tiers.


### Intercom


**Best for:** International companies that work in multiple languages.


[Intercom](https://www.intercom.com/) includes an omnichannel inbox and a unified service hub with automated workflows powered by its Fin AI agent, which can resolve customer issues autonomously. Most importantly, it’s the only option on our list that can automatically translate messages in[over 150 languages](https://www.intercom.com/app-store/apps/translate-g0fg) , so it’s a strong option for B2B companies expanding into international markets who aren’t ready to hire language specialists.


You may need to manually intercept the Fin AI, which doesn’t always automatically route queries to support teams when it doesn’t know an answer. While it’s meant to lift some of the manual workload off support teams, this extra step means your team may spend just as much time monitoring the AI agent as they did answering those queries in the first place, so it’s not a great fit for teams in the process of scaling.


Intercom is a relatively expensive option, and like several other platforms on this list, its per-outcome AI agent fees make costs difficult to predict.


## What to evaluate in a Help Scout alternative


Single issue in Pylon


Here’s what to look for as you evaluate Help Scout competitors and choose the best fit for your team:


- **Native Slack/Teams support.** Choose an omnichannel platform that includes native support for Slack and Microsoft Teams (and any other channels you use), so your support team can manage all customer conversations without switching inboxes.
- **Agentic scope.** Not every AI agent can use the same workflows or interact with your customers in the same way. Consider how often you’ll need to use the tool across teams and systems, and how much customization each tool offers.
- **Predictable AI pricing.** Look for a scalable pricing plan that includes bundle deals or unlimited AI resolutions. If you pay per resolution, your costs can escalate as quickly as your volume grows.
- **Advanced analytics.** Upgrades from Help Scout should include AI-powered tools that safely surface information from your own documentation to give you deep insights into your operational trends, as well as account context and team KPIs.
- **Cross-team visibility.** Just because everyone can see the same messages doesn’t mean they’re working from the same context. Every program you consider should be able to keep every team member informed of progress during each step of the resolution process, whether they’re an engineer or a[customer success](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-success-vs-customer-support) lead.
- **Account-level context.** As your team replies to customer queries, make sure they can see relevant context, like account health indicators and repeat concerns, without having to switch to a different app. AI agents can help gather this information if it’s not immediately available, like during a conversation on Slack.
- **Structured data migration and onboarding support.** Make sure it’s easy for your team to migrate data from Help Scout to the new platform, including historical tickets and internal notes.

## FAQ


### What’s the best Help Scout alternative for AI customer support?


All of the Help Scout competitors we’ve profiled in this article offer strong AI-powered tools for customer support. The best fit for your team depends on what exactly you need the AI tool to do and how much customer context you need to get that work done. Also, consider your growth plan: for many AI customer support tools, cost scales with usage. Scaling B2B teams that need to surface relevant customer context from a rich history while retaining a human touch to the support itself should consider Pylon.


### When should I choose Help Scout instead of an alternative?


Choose Help Scout if you have a small support team, most of your customer conversations are simple email inquiries, and you need a shared inbox, knowledge base, and[ticketing system](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/best-ticketing-systems-for-startups) that’s easy for your team to set up and use.


### What are Help Scout’s main limitations?


Help Scout’s main limitations are its lack of true omnichannel support for B2B channels like Slack and Teams, its basic analytics, and its limited features for complex issues involving multiple steps and teams.


### Can I migrate my Help Scout data to a new tool?


Yes. Help Scout[provides APIs](https://docs.helpscout.com/article/466-data-export-options) to help you export your conversation history, reporting data, customer list, and knowledge base articles. You can then import that data into a new tool, although you may need to do some customization to fit the new tool’s requirements.
